messages:
incident-bot: Paging @ashok (oncall) — elevated 429s and latency from /v1/embeddings across multiple zones, auto-alert triggered. Incident ID INC-2419. Please investigate.

ashok (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a sudden spike in embed ingestion from a handful of customers, ~10k RPS sustained on embeddings-write. preliminary: KV cache pressure and some backend shaper rules saturated.

rafael (infra): logs show token-serving queue growth at the redis layer, CPU on the tokenizer fleet at 92%. Most requests are small (<= 128 tokens) but super parallel.

maria (platform): quick customer impact: about 3 customers seeing >40% request failures (429 / 504), ~600 tenants with increased latencies. Not all customers—some traffic patterns are triggering our batching to explode.

ashok (oncall): action plan proposal: 1) apply temporary soft rate-limit on embedding create for heavy tenants, 2) enable shaper to cap concurrency by product-route, 3) disable nonessential server-side batching (experimental "bulk-embed-v2" path) to reduce KV churn. Requesting infra to run the shaper command.

rafael (infra): ready. will run a soft-shape first (no hard reject), then escalate to soft reject if not helpful. Command I'll run: ``shaper apply --scope=product:embeddings --selector=bulk-embed-v2 --mode=soft --rate=80/s --concurrency=8``. Executing in 2m.

ashok (oncall): +1. Also we should increase per-tenant short-term quotas for affected customers to avoid downstream errors while we shape overall. maria, can you list top affected tenants?

maria (platform): sending list to thread DM. Top 3 do we want to bump by 2x for 30m?

elaine (support): yes please. I'll draft a support note immediately and open tickets for those 3. We'll offer recommended client changes (backoff + reduce concurrency) until we stabilize.

jess (devex): I'll prepare an SDK advisory and quick code snippets. Proposal for client guidance: - honor 429 Retry-After if present - implement exponential backoff with jitter - add idempotency tokens for create calls (embeddings) - cap parallel requests per-host to 6 by default

sam (oncall): Recommended backoff params we've used before: base_delay=500ms, factor=2, max_delay=10000ms, attempts=6, jitter=0.1. Also recommend clients reduce batch size to 1-4 for embeddings until backend healthy.

jess (devex): posting quick JS/Python snippets here. JS: ```js // exponential backoff with jitter
async function backoff(attempt){
  const base = 500;
  const max = 10000;
  const factor = 2;
  let delay = Math.min(max, Math.floor(base * Math.pow(factor, attempt)));
  // add full jitter
  delay = Math.random() * delay;
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
}
```

jess (devex): Python: ```py import random, time

def backoff(attempt, base=0.5, factor=2, max_delay=10):
    delay = min(max_delay, base * (factor ** attempt))
    delay = random.random() * delay  # full jitter
    time.sleep(delay)
```

ashok (oncall): Also add idempotency guidance: for clients that do multi-part batch uploads create an idempotency token per logical batch, retry only safe idempotent endpoints, and ensure server returns a stable operation id.

maria (platform): rolling the shaper now, starting at 80/s soft on bulk-embed-v2 for 10m then re-evaluate. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood.example/d/shaper/embeddings?panelId=embed_queue

ops-bot: shaper job started by rafael. JobID sh-2419-01.

rafael (infra): metrics after 3m: queue depth down 45%, 429s dropped 30%, token queue CPU down to 68%. Latency still elevated for some tenants.

ashok (oncall): good. next step: disable server-side bulk-embed-v2 immediate path for non-critical customers to avoid cache thrash. Maria, can you set the feature flag rollout to off for non-enterprise tenants?

maria (platform): doing that now: ``ff toggles set bulk-embed-v2 --env=prod --off --scope=non-enterprise``. Change applied.

elaine (support): drafting customer messages now. For core affected customers we'll offer temporary quota bump + recommended client config (backoff + reduce concurrency). Anyone want to review the wording?

jess (devex): I'll add a short snippet for how to send an idempotency token in the SDK headers: ``Idempotency-Key: <uuid4>`` and recommend server error handling for 409 vs 200 responses.

sam (oncall): operational note: we should push a small SDK patch to reduce default parallelism for embeddings to 6 and include the backoff defaults. That reduces new customers from exacerbating this. Who owns the release? devex?

jess (devex): I can cut a micro release for the JS and Python SDKs with the new defaults. Will target a canary release in 30m.

ashok (oncall): customer impact check: maria+elaine, please confirm which accounts still seeing >10% failure after 15m. If >2 accounts still affected, we'll open a follow-up incident for client outreach.

maria (platform): After 12m: two accounts still at ~12% failure, both enterprise. I've requested a 2x quota bump for them for 1 hour.

elaine (support): support tickets created and messages sent to those customers; offering a call if they want.

rafael (infra): follow-up metrics: overall 429s back to baseline for non-enterprise. Enterprise traffic still higher due to long-running fanout jobs. Recommending targeted throttle rules for those tenant IDs: ``shaper apply --scope=tenant:12345 --rate=40/s --mode=soft``

ashok (oncall): agree. Apply targeted tenant shape and keep global soft limits. Also set alert to auto-escalate if causal 500s appear.

ops-bot: applied tenant shape sh-2419-02 by rafael.

ashok (oncall): post-mortem actions (short): 1) enforce default client concurrency drop in next SDK release (jess) 2) add server-side defensive quota fallback to reject early with clear Retry-After vs queueing 3) evaluate bulk-embed-v2 batching logic for cache churn (rafael + infra) 4) improve dashboard alerts to detect batching pattern anomalies (maria).

jess (devex): noted. I'll include the guidance and code snippets in a short KB article and link to it from the support replies.

ashok (oncall): status: incident moved to mitigated at +25m. Keeping this thread open for follow-ups. Great work. :tada:
